extracted.intended_audience: educational institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, disability services staff, and legal/compliance counsel responsible for Title IX implementation
extracted.subtask_description: Interpreting and implementing Title IX requirements for providing reasonable modifications, leaves, and related supports to students who are pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions, including the role of the recipient and Title IX Coordinator. Focused on compliance steps, individualized determinations, and examples of reasonable and unreasonable modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility to take prompt and effective steps upon notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Title IX Coordinator is notified of a student's pregnancy or related conditions, the recipient always remains responsible for taking prompt and effective steps to prevent sex discrimination, including provision of reasonable modifications, leave, and lactation space (see §106.40(b)(3) and §106.44).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps will vary based on facts and circumstances; may include use of grievance procedures under §106.45 (and §106.46 for certain postsecondary harassment situations), coordination of remedies, supportive measures to restore or preserve access in absence of a complaint or during grievance procedures, and other timely actions. Recipients must respond promptly and effectively under §106.44(a) and (f)(1) when knowledge of conduct that may constitute sex discrimination arises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility to provide information about recipient obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must provide information to the student about the recipient's obligations under §§106.40(b)(1) through (5) and 106.44(j), in addition to the notice of nondiscrimination under §106.8(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement can be satisfied in a single conversation or, if appropriate to the student's age/ability, by standardized written communication. The added title 'Responsibility to provide information about recipient obligations' aims to help readers locate this topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide reasonable modifications for pregnancy-related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must make reasonable modifications to its policies, practices, or procedures as necessary to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access to the recipient's education program or activity (§106.40(b)(3)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifications must be based on each student's individualized needs. The requirement is separate from, and in addition to, the recipient's obligation to provide voluntary leave (§106.40(b)(3)(iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for providing reasonable modifications – individualized consultative process
rubrics_metrics.description: When a student notifies the Title IX Coordinator that they are pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions, the recipient must consult with the student to determine the student's individualized needs and offer options that will best prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access (§106.40(b)(3)(ii)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The student is not required to identify or request a specific modification; identifying a reasonable modification is a collaborative effort. The recipient must offer reasonable modifications and, if accepted by the student, promptly and effectively implement them. The recipient may choose to offer one or more preferred options when multiple reasonable modifications exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student discretion and voluntary acceptance of modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: A student has discretion whether to accept or decline an offered modification; a student cannot be required to accept a particular modification (§106.40(b)(3)(ii)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the student declines an offered reasonable modification that would meet their individualized needs, the recipient is not required to propose other reasonable modifications for that specific need unless new or additional needs arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental alteration standard – not a reasonable modification
rubrics_metrics.description: A modification that a recipient can demonstrate would fundamentally alter the nature of its education program or activity is not a reasonable modification (§106.40(b)(3)(ii)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient bears the burden of demonstrating a fundamental alteration. Jurisprudence and examples show that waiving requirements that demonstrate mastery, jeopardizing accreditation, or waiving clinical/competency requirements may constitute fundamental alterations. By contrast, deferments, make-up exams, tutoring, seating changes, or allowing untimed exams are typically reasonable. Demonstrating a fundamental alteration does not relieve the recipient of its obligation to consult with the student and otherwise offer reasonable modifications that prevent discrimination and ensure access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive, non-exhaustive list of example reasonable modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Section §106.40(b)(3)(ii)(C) provides examples of reasonable modifications (the list 'may include but is not limited to' and is non-exhaustive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include intermittent absences to attend medical appointments (and related make-up opportunities), lactation breaks and lactation space, breaks to eat/drink/use restroom, allowing a student to sit/stand or carry water, larger desks, online instruction (clarified that online need not be 'homebound'), switching to comparable afternoon sections, tutoring, supplemental instruction, academic counseling, homework assistance, changes in course load, and modifications in athletic/extracurricular contexts. Whether a particular modification is reasonable is fact-specific and individualized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between reasonable modifications and voluntary leave of absence
rubrics_metrics.description: The obligation to provide reasonable modifications (§106.40(b)(3)(ii)) is separate and distinct from the longstanding obligation to provide a voluntary leave of absence for pregnancy or related conditions (§106.40(b)(3)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a student's requested leave exceeds the framework provided in §106.40(b)(3)(iv), the excess should be considered a request for a reasonable modification under §106.40(b)(3)(ii). Commenters asked for clarification on intermittent absences vs. leave; the Department declined to move intermittent absences out of the reasonable modifications provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient burden to demonstrate unreasonableness or fundamental alteration
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient has the burden of demonstrating that a particular or requested modification would fundamentally alter the nature of its education program or activity or is otherwise unreasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a recipient demonstrates fundamental alteration for one requested modification, it must still consult with the student and consider/offers other reasonable modifications tailored to the student's needs, and implement any accepted reasonable modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator role – coordination and oversight, recipient responsible for implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient—not the Title IX Coordinator—is ultimately responsible for implementing requests for reasonable modifications; the Title IX Coordinator must coordinate actions and retain oversight to ensure consistent compliance under Title IX and the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may delegate specific duties to other departments (e.g., disability services, academic affairs, campus health) as appropriate, but the Title IX Coordinator retains ultimate oversight. The regulations permit coordination/consultation with disability services, Section 504 teams, or IEP teams where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and effective implementation and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reasonable modification is offered and accepted by the student, the recipient must promptly and effectively implement the modification; prior proposals expected coordination and documentation by the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations clarify the recipient's responsibility to take actions and the Title IX Coordinator's responsibility to coordinate; documentation and effective implementation were reasons commenters supported strong Title IX Coordinator involvement. Promptness and timeliness (including addressing concerns about timeliness) are emphasized under §106.40(b)(3) and §106.40(b)(3)(i).
